Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *ɡeːns): semantic 玉 (“jade”) + phonetic 見 (OC *keːns, *ɡeːns) — to appear.
Stativized form of the transitive verb 見 (OC *keːns, “to see”), formed by a nasal prefix and expressing the sense "to be visible; to appear" (Mei, 2012).

evidence.text: This page analyzes 現 as a phono-semantic graph with 玉 as semantic element and 見 as sound element, and gives the Old Chinese forms Zhengzhang *ɡeːns and Baxter–Sagart *N-[k]ˤen-s. It separately reports a proposal, attributed to Mei (2012), that the “be visible; appear” verb is a nasal-prefix stativized form of transitive 見 ‘see.’ The page also reports the competing account that 現 first wrote a word meaning ‘jade luster’ and was later borrowed for the word ‘appear.’ These are source-reported analyses; this page alone does not establish the relative chronology of those lexical uses.

evidence.field: Glyph origin; Etymology; Middle Chinese and Old Chinese readings
evidence.text: The page likewise identifies 玉 as semantic and 見 as phonetic, lists 見-series comparisons in Zhengzhang’s system, and gives 現 as Zhengzhang *ɡeːns and Baxter–Sagart *N-[k]ˤen-s, versus 見 *keːns/*ɡeːns. It reports Middle Chinese henH, fanqie 胡甸切, and cites Mei (2012) for the nasal-prefix stative analysis. The two OC notations belong to distinct reconstruction systems and should not be merged. The packet’s exact local Baxter–Sagart row for 現 agrees with *N-[k]ˤen-s; no external Baxter–Sagart primary table row was verified here.

evidence.field: 現: basic and detailed explanation, cited lexicographic entries
evidence.text: The entry gives 現 as a phono-semantic graph, with 玉 as semantic element and 見 as sound element, and glosses the verb as ‘appear; become visible.’ It separately records noun senses ‘jade luster’ and ‘stone inferior to jade,’ citing 集韻, and cites 廣韻 for “現，俗見字.” It also supplies later examples for ‘appear,’ ‘current,’ and ‘on hand,’ including a Southern Liang quotation for a ‘current/present’ use. These are dictionary-reported senses and examples, not a demonstrated chronology of semantic change.

evidence.text: This secondary entry identifies 玉 as semantic and 見 as phonetic, lists 現 and 見 among a 見 phonetic series, and gives Zhengzhang Old Chinese 現 *ɡeːns versus 見 *keːns, *ɡeːns. It also reports Mei (2012)’s analysis of 現 ‘be visible; appear’ as a nasal-prefix stative form of transitive 見 ‘see.’ The entry presents an analysis, not dated evidence establishing that derivation or its chronology.
evidence.title: 現 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.field: 《康熙字典》 citations; 《說文》 cross-reference; phonology
evidence.text: The entry reports 《集韻》’s glosses 玉光 (‘jade luster’) and 石之次玉者 (‘stone inferior to jade’), 《正韻》’s 顯也、露也 (‘manifest; reveal’), and cites 抱朴子 for 形現往來. It explicitly says 現 is not a headword in 《說文》 and points instead to 見, whose gloss is 視也 (‘to look/see’). It reports Middle Chinese 匣母 霰韻 去聲, 見小韻, 胡甸切 for 現. These citations document dictionary traditions and reported usage; this page does not provide dated early attestations or settle whether the jade gloss preceded the ‘appear’ word.

gaps: No inspected paleographic catalogue or excavated inscription establishes the earliest form or earliest dated graphic occurrence of 現. The retrieved sources do not justify asserting an oracle-bone, bronze, or seal-form developmental sequence for this graph.

The relative chronology of the lexemes glossed ‘jade luster’ and ‘appear/be visible’ remains unsettled here. A secondary source reports both a phonetic-loan account and Mei’s nasal-prefix stative derivation from 見; primary dated attestations establishing either pathway were not inspected.

The quoted 《祖庭事苑》 passage is available only through a search result; its page could not be opened, so its text, context, edition, and date were not verified. The Chinese Text Project search result also did not preserve usable date and sense boundaries.

Exact official Unicode Unihan page for U+73FE was attempted but returned an internal error. The supplied local Unihan row says 現 xiàn, but this does not satisfy character-specific external verification. The U+73B0 official page confirms 现 xiàn and identifies 現 as its traditional variant.

Local Baxter–Sagart table row provided in the input gives 現 MC henH and OC *N-[k]ˤen-s. The external page gives the same OC form and contrasts 見 *keːns/*ɡeːns, but the component’s exact local table row was not included in the packet and no official upstream data file was inspected; the host reconstruction alone does not prove the historical phonetic relationship.

A meaningful 玉 semantic role is plausible and supported as a component analysis by secondary references, but the ministry reference inspected establishes only 玉’s general jade meaning, not why it was selected in 現. No source verified possible graphic corruption or an alternative early graph.
No source on reuse terms for any recurring online source was reviewed; no local extract or mirrored text is recommended.

The dictionary cites separate senses and later literary examples, but no early dated corpus contexts were verified to establish the first use of either lexeme or a borrowing pathway.

The proposed nasal-prefix stative relationship between 現 ‘appear’ and 見 ‘see’ is reported from Mei (2012) by a secondary source; the primary argument was not inspected. It remains a competing analysis, not an established semantic chronology.

The modern reading xiàn for 現 is supplied by the local Unihan row, but the official U+73FE endpoint returned an internal error. U+73B0’s official record confirms 现 xiàn and its traditional variant relationship. No usable character-specific official Unihan record for 見 was obtained during this pass, and the packet lacks its local Unihan and Baxter–Sagart rows; therefore no paired current or Baxter–Sagart component/host reading comparison is asserted.

The local Baxter–Sagart row gives 現 *N-[k]ˤen-s and MC henH, but no 見 row was supplied. The inspected secondary entry instead gives Zhengzhang’s distinct-system comparison 現 *ɡeːns and 見 *keːns/*ɡeːns. These notations must not be merged; neither the local host row alone nor the Zhengzhang comparison proves a Baxter–Sagart sound relationship.
